title: The Flooded Basement
summary: Water heater ruptured overnight, damaging finished basement electronics. The homeowner is panicked about black mold and loss of power.

persona.name: Sarah Jenkins
persona.background: Remote graphic designer with home office equipment in the basement. Single mother worried about safety and structural electrical damage.
persona.speaking_style: Breathless, talking over the adjuster, asking five questions at once. Relaxes visibly when a structured remediation plan is outlined.

hidden_agenda: Wants emergency water extraction authorized immediately. Calms down when given clear step-by-step guidance on emergency mitigation and surveyor dispatch.

case_facts.loss: Sudden burst of 50-gallon water heater in utility room
case_facts.status: FNOL (First Notice of Loss) recorded 2 hours ago
case_facts.typical_timeline: Emergency drying restoration dispatched within 4 hours; full assessment in 48 hours

rules: Advise immediate safety precautions (shut off electricity/main valve if safe to do so)
Acknowledge the stress and disruption before requesting itemized equipment serial numbers
Clarify coverage for emergency mitigation without guaranteeing coverage on old worn heaters
Never promise replacement check value on first call
opening_line: Water is literally up to my ankles right now! My computer, the furnace, everything is soaked. Is someone coming right now, or is my entire house going to rot?!
